يتم تركيب خيمة على منطقة الحفر

تأكد من فصل التيار الكهربائى عن الكابل من الجهتين

لا تلمس أو تمسك أو تحرك بيدك أي كابل يسري به الطاقة الكهربية

 ضرر مرافق اخرى مثل توصيلات المياه والمجارى والتليفونات والغاز وعند اكتشاف

 لنوعية التربية مع وضع حواجز خشبية لمنع الانهيار اذا لزم الامر
 ايقاف العمل فى الحفر فورا عند ظهور غازات او تدفق مياه 
 وبحث اسباب ظهورها
 عند وجود كابل اخر فى مسار الحفر او ظهور اكثر من كابل 
 اثناء الحفر يجب ان يتم العمل فى حضور المشرف على العمل والا يتم اى عمل الا بتوجيه 
 منه

 يحظر استعمال الاليات فى الحفر عند ظهور الكابل او اى دلالة على وجود كابل او اى مرافق اخرى تحت الارض ويتم استكمال الحفر يدويا

Maintenance Procedure Information System

Document No.: Cable-003-r0a | Equipment: Medium Voltage Cables 12/20 kV XLPE
Issued to: 
 Distribution Companies
Status:

Approval date: 
 05 February 2007 | Procedure: Installation of Premolded Joint Box
Next review date: February 
 2012
Introduction
This document sets out the steps for installing premolded (Elastimold) joints for three-phase cables, 11 and 20 kV, according to the installation instructions supplied with the joint. This joint is designed to be a permanent, fully insulated and buryable joint. The joint withstands the voltage marked on the outside of the joint body and can withstand a current capacity equal to that borne by the cable. The joint is used with extruded and insulated cables (XLPE) OR (EPR), using copper or aluminium ferrules according to the cable type. The document was discussed and approved on 05 February 2007 by the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions
Issue a work permit and an approved work order; maintenance personnel must carry the occupational safety and health category card. | 
Failure to follow these instructions precisely may cause damage to the joint and serious or fatal injuries. | 
Erect a temporary fence to mark the excavation area, with appropriate warning signs, adding red illuminated signals or lanterns at night. | 
Joint parts shall be installed only by persons well trained in installation and in the safe use of high-voltage equipment, experienced in working on cables, and the work shall be carried out under the direct supervision of the work supervisor. | 
Erect a tent over the excavation area. | 
Ensure the power supply is disconnected from the cable from both sides and take measures to prevent reconnection. | 
Locate the fault using the special equipment for that purpose. | 
Disconnect the supply from the cables adjacent to the cable to be worked on at the fault locations during the excavation period. | 
Earth the cable to be worked on from both sides, with appropriate warning signs posted (Do not connect — workmen are working). | 
Inspect the contents of this joint to ensure they are complete and undamaged, and ensure they are fully compatible with the cables. | 
Do not touch, hold or move by hand any cable carrying electrical power. | 
Any excessive tampering with the joint components may cause it to fail. | 
Do not burn waste resulting from joint installation work; it must be collected and sent to the waste collection point for recycling. | 
When excavating at the fault location, observe the following:
 Obtain an excavation permit to ensure excavation will not damage other utilities such as water, sewerage, telephone and gas connections; if any of these utilities is found, excavation work shall be stopped until the characteristics of these utilities are established.
 Excavate according to technical practice, with the excavation slope suitable for the soil type, placing wooden barriers to prevent collapse if necessary.
 Stop excavation work immediately if gases appear or water flows, and investigate the causes.
 If another cable is in the excavation path, or more than one cable appears during excavation, work must be carried out in the presence of the work supervisor and no work shall be done except on his instructions.
 Provide suitable scaffolds for crossing the excavation if needed.
 The use of machinery in excavation is prohibited when the cable or any indication of a cable or any other underground utility appears; excavation shall be completed manually.
 After the work supervisor has satisfied himself of the cable to be worked on, using a signal generator, that the cable is dead and identified, he shall spike the cable at the point where cutting will take place, using an approved metal spike with an insulated handle (spiking tool) to short-circuit the cable conductors to earth, provided the spike is earthed before spiking; insulating gloves and safety goggles must be worn and the operator must stand on an insulating platform before starting the spiking operation. After spiking, ensure no other feeder has tripped as a result of the spiking, to confirm that the spiking was on the cable to be worked on and not on any other cable.
 If the fault has exposed all cable ends, a voltage indicator must be used to ensure absence of voltage.
 The cable armouring or its sheath may be used as an earth.
If it becomes necessary to move live cables, observe the following:
 When moving the part of the cable near the end boxes, ensure these boxes are well fixed.
 Wear tar-impregnated cloth gloves over the insulating gloves during this work.
 The work shall be carried out by workers experienced in working on cables and under the direct supervision of the work supervisor.
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Tool bag
Press and suitable set of dies
Metal spike with insulated handle ('spiking tool')
Butagas cylinder and welding torch
Sharpener, saw, cutter
Voltage indicator
Signal generator
Sufficient number of portable earths
Tent
Joint Box Contents
3 insulating tubes, 3 ferrules
PVC tape
2 outer sheaths
3 earth copper
Armouring and clamps (for armoured cables)
3 silicone grease, mastic tape
Cleaning liquid, sandpaper
Tin solder or spring clip
Procedures to be Carried Out
First: Cable Preparation
Align the two cable ends to be connected in one straight line | 1.
Leave a common distance (Overlap) of 150 mm between the two ends as shown in the drawing | 2.
Insert the first and second outer protection tubes around cable No. (1) | 3.
Second: Removing the Sheath and Armouring
Remove the outer sheath of one end for 800 mm from the centre of the joint and the other end for 500 mm from the centre of the joint | 1.
For armoured cables: | 2.
- Remove the armouring to the same dimensions as the outer sheath for each of the two ends | 
- Remove the inner sheath, leaving 10 mm after the armouring, carefully so as not to scratch the copper tape under the inner sheath | 
- Insert a clamp in both ends (1, 2) to bind the armouring afterwards | 
Remove the filling from both ends | 3.
Mark and identify each pair of opposite phases to be connected according to the phase markings, and cut the excess at the centre of the joint | 4.
Note: The position in which the excess is cut is the same position in which the ferrule is installed, to ensure the dimensions do not exceed those permitted in the table (before and after crimping).
Third: Preparing the Phases
Insert the copper stocking on the phase on the side of cable No. (1) | 1.
Remove the copper tape carefully for 200 mm — see table (Y + 30 mm) — from the end of cable (2), for a length (Z) from the end of cable (1), taking care not to scratch the outer semiconducting layer of the cable | 2.
Remove the outer semiconducting layer carefully (with a suitable tool) from both cable ends for 150 mm — see table (Y) — to obtain a smooth, even surface, with the end of the outer semiconducting layer uniformly rounded and tapered | 3.
Remove the XLPE insulation for 55 mm (X) — see table — making a bevelled cone shape in the insulation at its start (Bevel) for 10 mm | 4.
Warning: Do not cut or do anything that would damage the insulation layer, the semiconducting layer or any part of the conductor, as it may damage or reduce the expected life of the conductor.

Fourth: Applying the Welding Tape
Clean the XLPE insulation of the phase of cable No. 1 with the cleaning liquid and cleaning pieces, in the direction of the arrow, ensuring it is sound and free of any defects or scratches | 1.
Wrap a layer of welding tape on the end of the conductor of cable No. (1) to protect the joint (Housing) during entry | 2.
Cover the outer semiconducting layer of the phase of cable No. (1) R1, S1, T1 with welding tape, starting the wrap from the start of the copper tape inwards until reaching the XLPE insulation, as in the drawing | 3.
Fifth: Inserting the Joint
Ensure the conductor and the XLPE insulation and the welding tape on the phase of cable No. (1) are clean before the Housing insulation enters | 1.
Apply silicone grease on the insulation and the welding tape for one of the phases of cable No. (1), as in the drawing | 2.
Insert the Housing insulator by pressing with a slight twist in the direction of the welding tape wrap until the XLPE insulation of the cable appears for approximately 10 mm on the same phase used in the previous step | 3.
Repeat steps 2 and 3 for each phase separately | 4.
Sixth: Installing the Ferrules
Remove the PVC welding tape from the end of the conductor of cable No. (1) | 1.
Insert the ferrule in each of the two phases | 2.
Check the dimensions (before crimping) so that the distance between the two insulation ends does not exceed 127 mm | 3.
Crimp the ferrule; check the dimensions (after crimping) so that the distance between the two insulation ends does not exceed 132 mm, and if the distance exceeds this, the preparation must be repeated and another ferrule crimped | 4.
Remove impurities and sharp protrusions from the ferrule and make its surface smooth and clean | 5.
Seventh: Installing the Joint
Clean the XLPE insulation with the cleaning liquid and cleaning pieces (cleaning is always in the direction of the arrows) | 1.
Grease the surface of the insulation and the conductor with the supplied silicone grease for one phase only | 2.
Pull the Housing insulator into the opposite phase (cable No. 2) by pulling with a slight twist until the start of the welding tape of the phase of cable No. (1) appears; remove it to expose the outer semiconducting layer on cable No. (1) for 50 mm, leaving the rest of the tape, then grease the exposed insulation distance | 3.
Pull the Housing insulator to the final position so that the overlapping part of the insulator on the outer semiconducting layer of the phase from both ends is equal; this is noticed by touch or sight from the occurrence of a clear high lip at the end of the outer semiconducting layer on the surface of the insulator, as in the drawing | 4.
Repeat steps 2, 3 and 4 for each phase separately | 5.
Step 3: Remove 50 mm from the insulation tape — Remove 50 mm from the PVC tape
Step 4: Final Position — Final Position
Eighth: Restoring the Copper Tape
Pull the earth copper mesh, spread it and bind it to the copper tape from both sides, using only the spring clip or copper wire, and solder with tin carefully so as not to affect the outer semiconducting layer of the cable under the copper tape | 1.
Assemble the phases using adhesive tape along the joint so that the assembly diameter is as small as possible | 2.
Ninth: Restoring the Armouring for Armoured Cables
Peel the outer sheath from both ends for 75 mm to suit the armouring length | 1.
Bind the two armouring ends with the clamps | 2.
Wrap mastic tape over the clamps from both ends | 3.
Wrap adhesive tape over the armouring so that the assembly diameter is as small as possible | 4.
Tenth: Restoring the Outer Sheath
Roughen the outer sheath of both cables for 100 mm and wrap mastic tape over it | 1.
Pull the outer protection tube and adjust its position so that it covers 90 mm of the outer sheath of cable No. (1); shrink it using the appropriate flame | 2.
Wrap mastic tape over the inner end of the previous tube for 100 mm | 3.
Pull the second protection tube and adjust its position so that it covers 200 mm of the outer end of cable No. 2 and approximately 150 mm on the inner end of the first tube; shrink it as before, from outside to inside | 4.
Record the joint box data in the cable register |
